name: Groq API token pricing (serverless LPU, per 1M tokens, 2026-10-04 list price)
region: Groq cloud (US); no regional GPU SKU to price
price_basis: USD per 1M TOKENS, LIST PRICE, observed 2026-10-04. openai/gpt-oss-20b $0.075 input / $0.30 output at 1000 tok/s; openai/gpt-oss-120b $0.15 / $0.60 at 500 tok/s; qwen/qwen3.8-27b $0.80 / $4.00 at 450 tok/s; openai/safety-gpt-oss-20b $0.075 / $0.30. Speech is priced by time not tokens: whisper-large-v3 $0.111 per hour, whisper-large-v3-turbo $0.04 per hour. Content-moderation models are priced per 1M tokens AND per 1M CHARACTERS on the same page (Canopy Labs Orpheus V1 English $22.00 per 1M characters, Arabic Saudi $40.00). price_usd = gpt-oss-20b input.
notes: Two things make Groq's page structurally different from the others. First, its headline Llama models are NOT on the public list price at all: llama-3.1-8b-instant and llama-3.3-70b-versatile both read literally 'ContactSales' in the price column. So the cheapest commonly-quoted Groq number in circulation is stale - Llama 3.3 70B on Groq moved to sales-gated pricing, and only the gpt-oss / Qwen / guard models remain self-serve. Second, Groq publishes SPEED next to price on the same row (1000 and 500 tok/s for the gpt-oss models), which makes it the only provider here where throughput is a published list attribute rather than something you benchmark yourself. For character-priced models, tokens are the wrong unit - $22 per 1M CHARACTERS on a TTS-style model is not comparable to a $2 per 1M token input rate at all. No GPU hourly rate is published.
